newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Korea says Seoul army shakeup exposes war plans.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea says Seoul army shakeup exposes war plans.

text.p: North Korea said on Saturday a reshuffle in the South Korean military showed Seoul was preparing for war with the north.

Seoul's appointment of Kim Dong-jin to replace Lee Yang-ho as Defence Minister, announced on Thursday, revealed plans by South Korea to bolster its war preparations, Pyongyang said in a communique, carried by its official KCNA news agency.
"The reshuffle came at a time when the...war-maniacs were making a fuss over 'provocations' from the north and manoeuvring for all-out confrontation," the communique said.
"This reveals their intention to step up war preparations against the north."

Seoul and communist Pyongyang swapped threats earlier this month following the incursion of a North Korean submarine that set ashore 26 agents in an east coast area after striking rocks on September 18.
Twenty-two of the 26 agents were killed by southern troops or found dead. One was captured alive and soldiers are searching the east coast for the remaining three.

Seoul has branded the incident a provocation, while Pyongyang maintains the submarine drifted into the south after encountering engine trouble and has threatened "merciless retaliation" for the deaths of its soldiers.

On Friday, Seoul's new defence chief pledged to lead a force strong enough to "win every war", but he blamed Pyongyang for raising tensions on the peninsula, where a fragile ceasefire has kept the peace since the 1950-53 Korean War.
